_description: Reproducible behaviour worth a future debugger's time: symptoms seen, root cause found, fix applied. Includes recurring footguns (the footgun IS the symptom). Append only; prefer a new entry over editing when understanding evolves.

title: Vite serves a stale module after container recreate or new lib export
symptoms: Uncaught SyntaxError: does not provide an export named X
504 Outdated Optimize Dep
UI renders old markup after a source change
root_cause: Vite keeps a pre-optimized dependency graph in node_modules/.vite; the running dev server serves it even after the source changed.
fix: Clear node_modules/.vite in the container and 'docker compose up -d --force-recreate app', then hard-refresh the browser.

title: Carbon silently overflows out-of-range dates and throws on garbage
symptoms: Imported asset lands in the wrong year (e.g. 2026-13-99 becomes 2027-04-09)
Uncaught exception on an unparseable date string
root_cause: Carbon::createFromFormat('Y-m-d', ...) overflows invalid date parts instead of rejecting, and throws (not returns null) on unparseable input.
fix: Validate by round-tripping: reject when $date->format('Y-m-d') !== input; wrap in try/catch and skip on throw. See parseDate() in ImportCsv.

title: Test suite could wipe the real dev DB via container env vars
symptoms: RefreshDatabase pointed at the bind-mounted dev database instead of in-memory
root_cause: The container exports DB_CONNECTION/DB_DATABASE as process env, which override phpunit.xml and .env.testing.
fix: tests/TestCase.php::createApplication() forces database.default=sqlite and :memory: at boot. Do not remove this override.

title: European decimal format mis-parsed on CSV import
symptoms: Imported value 1.234,56 stored as 1.234 (off by ~1000x)
Export/import round-trip changes amounts
root_cause: Naive str_replace(',', '.') ignores the thousands separator; export writes number_format(v, 2, ',', '.').
fix: Detect the rightmost of '.'/',' as the decimal separator and strip the other as thousands. See parseDecimal() in ImportCsv.

title: Scheduled prices:fetch never ran — schedule defined but no runner
symptoms: Live prices only update on the manual 'Aggiorna prezzi' button
fetched_at stays at the last manual refresh despite a daily 06:00 schedule
root_cause: routes/console.php defines Schedule::command('prices:fetch')->dailyAt('06:00'), but the container start command and composer dev ran serve/queue/pail/vite without 'php artisan schedule:work', so nothing executed the schedule.
fix: Add 'php artisan schedule:work' to the concurrently process list in docker-compose.yml and composer.json (dev). Verify with a standalone schedule:work process in the container and 'php artisan schedule:list'.

title: Http::fake() called twice doesn't replace the first stub; fakeSequence + retry() consumes extra items
symptoms: A second Http::fake() in one test still returns the first stub's response
A test using fakeSequence with a client that has ->retry() exhausts the sequence and the request 500s/throws
root_cause: Http::fake() merges stubs rather than replacing; retry() makes multiple requests that each pull a sequence item.
fix: Per test, set one Http::fake with a wildcard, or seed DB state directly instead of chaining two fakes. Avoid fakeSequence when the client retries, or push enough items to cover attempts.

title: A newly added queued Job never runs in the dev container
symptoms: A freshly dispatched job sits in the jobs table with attempts=0, reserved_at=null and is never picked up
UI that polls job-produced state stays stuck (e.g. Scalable in-app login frozen on 'Avvio del login in corso…')
php artisan queue:restart appears to do nothing
root_cause: The container's queue:listen worker (started by the docker-compose dev command via concurrently) has been running since the container was last (re)created. It predates the new Job class added afterwards, so its loaded code/autoloader doesn't know the class and it silently fails to process it. queue:restart under the concurrently wrapper does not reliably respawn the child worker.
fix: Recreate the app container so the worker restarts on current code: `docker compose up -d --force-recreate app`. The CLI session (scalable-cli volume) and the SQLite DB (bind-mount) survive. Diagnosis trick: `php artisan queue:work --once` processes the stuck job immediately — proving the code is fine and the stale long-running worker is the culprit. Does not occur in prod, where a deploy recreates the container.

title: queue:listen kills the 900s Scalable login job at 60s with ProcessTimedOutException
symptoms: [queue] Symfony ProcessTimedOutException: the queue:work --once process exceeded the timeout of 60 seconds
queue process exits code 1 under concurrently right after dispatching RunScalableCliLogin
in-app Scalable login dies around a minute in
root_cause: queue:listen spawns each job as a queue:work --once subprocess and wraps it with its own --timeout (default 60s). RunScalableCliLogin blocks up to 900s polling the device-code login, so the listener's 60s subprocess timeout kills it long before the job's own $timeout=900. The composer dev script and the docker-compose start command both ran queue:listen --tries=1 with no --timeout.
fix: Pass --timeout=910 (>= the job's 900s) to queue:listen in both composer.json (dev) and docker-compose.yml, then recreate the container: docker compose up -d --force-recreate app.

title: Snapshot net worth exceeds sum of current-month asset rows
symptoms: 'Snapshot patrimonio' total differs from 'Valori del mese' by a fixed amount
difference equals one category's value (e.g. Fondo Pensione)
root_cause: ComputeValuesAsOf::latestKnownValue takes each category's most recent row on-or-before the date, so a category with no row in the current month is carried forward from an earlier month and still counts toward net worth. The current-month sum omits it; the snapshot includes it. Not a bug — intended so net worth doesn't drop just because a slow-moving asset (pension) wasn't re-entered this month.
fix: Surface it, don't hide it: BuildNetWorthReconciliation splits total into currentMonthTotal + carriedForward[] (category, value, asOf month), rendered as a reconciliation row on the InputData snapshot card via NetWorthReconciliation.tsx. Dashboard headline excludes illiquid categories so it does not show this gap.

title: ETF TER (expense_ratio) never backfills; AI advisor asks user to enter it
symptoms: expense_ratio NULL on all assets even for real ETFs
advisor context says 'nessun TER inserito' and tells user to add it
root_cause: Yahoo's fundProfile module is only populated on the exchange-suffixed symbol (ISAC.MI), not the bare ticker. FetchEtfPrice backfilled TER using only the symbol that returned a price — the bare ISAC — which yields NULL for fundProfile, so the TER was never stored.
fix: backfillExpenseRatio now iterates every price candidate (bare + .MI) and stops at the first non-null TER. TER then flows into ComputeAdvisorExtras -> RenderAdvisorContext.

title: Advisor chat/report reply never lands, chat spins on 'thinking' forever
symptoms: chat reply or report never appears; pending assistant bubble spins indefinitely
failed_jobs shows ContinueChatJob/GenerateAdvisorReportJob with MaxAttemptsExceededException despite tries=1
root_cause: config/queue.php database retry_after (was 90s) was shorter than the advisor jobs' 600s timeout. A local model taking >90s to reply let the queue consider the job abandoned and re-run it; with tries=1 the re-run immediately throws MaxAttemptsExceededException and the reply is lost. Golden rule: retry_after MUST exceed the longest job timeout.
fix: retry_after default raised to 660s (past the 600s job timeout). Added ContinueChatJob::failed() so a dead job flips a still-pending assistant turn to failed, instead of leaving the UI spinning.

title: Prism + Ollama returns 404 'Unknown error' — wrong endpoint path
symptoms: Prism calls against the Ollama provider fail with 'Ollama Error [404]: Unknown error'; PrismAdvisorProvider surfaces 'Il modello non ha risposto. Verifica la configurazione.'
root_cause: config('prism.providers.ollama.url') was set to the base URL plus '/v1' (an OpenAI-compatible-shim assumption). Prism's Ollama handler POSTs to the NATIVE 'api/chat' path relative to that url, so '/v1/api/chat' 404s.
fix: Set prism.providers.ollama.url to the bare base URL WITHOUT '/v1' (e.g. http://host.docker.internal:11434). AppServiceProvider points it at services.advisor.ollama.base_url. Prism appends 'api/chat' itself.

title: whereBetween on a date-cast column drops the lower-bound row when passed a Carbon
symptoms: A Snapshot::whereBetween('date', [$start->date, $end->date]) query returns one row FEWER than expected, always missing the row exactly on the lower bound. Surfaced as the networth_line advisor widget showing 2 points instead of 3 in a test.
root_cause: The snapshots.date column stores a bare date string ('2026-01-31'), but the model casts it 'date:Y-m-d' so $model->date is a Carbon at 00:00:00. Passing that Carbon into whereBetween stringifies it to '2026-01-31 00:00:00' (19 chars). SQLite compares the bound as text: the stored '2026-01-31' (10 chars) is lexicographically LESS than '2026-01-31 00:00:00', so the >= lower bound excludes it.
fix: Pass the bounds formatted to the column's own granularity: whereBetween('date', [$start->date->format('Y-m-d'), $end->date->format('Y-m-d')]). Rule: when filtering a date-only column, format Carbon bounds to Y-m-d — never rely on the default datetime stringification.

title: Advisor tool with date/relative-time params: give the model today's date and the data range in the tool description
symptoms: The net_worth_between advisor tool WAS called (the reply cited real figures) but produced a zero-length period ('due mesi fa' -> from==to, variazione +0,00€) and so emitted no networth_line widget. The model, not the code, was at fault.
root_cause: A local model (Llama-3.3 via Regolo) has no reliable notion of today's date or which dates actually have data, so a relative phrase like 'two months ago' resolves to a guessed date that collapses onto the same snapshot as 'now'.
fix: Inject concrete anchors into the tool description at build time: today's date (Carbon::now) and the tracked snapshot range (min/max snapshots.date), and state in the param descriptions that 'from' must be a PAST date, different from and before 'to'. General rule: any advisor tool taking dates or relative time must surface today + the valid range in its description, not assume the model knows them.

title: updateOrCreate with 'deleted_at' => null does not restore a soft-deleted row
symptoms: re-importing an item whose row was soft-deleted leaves deleted_at set
assertNotSoftDeleted fails after an idempotent re-import that should have restored the row
root_cause: deleted_at is not in the model's $fillable, so passing 'deleted_at' => null in updateOrCreate()'s values array is silently dropped by mass-assignment. The row matches and is updated, but stays soft-deleted. ImportScalableTransactions has the same latent pattern (untested for the trashed-restore case).
fix: Use withTrashed()->firstOrNew([key]), ->fill([...attrs]), then set $model->deleted_at = null explicitly, then ->save(). See ImportBankTransactions::importAccount.

title: Enable Banking 429 ASPSP_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: some banks allow only a few reads per account per day
symptoms: bank:import-transactions imports one account but silently skips another
last_sync_error 'Transazioni non disponibili' on an account whose connection is still active
a live probe of GET /accounts/{uid}/transactions returns HTTP 429 with error ASPSP_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
root_cause: PSD2 ASPSPs cap the consented access multiplicity per account per day. Some banks are permissive; others allow only a handful of reads/day. Debug probes plus repeated import runs exhaust the daily quota, and further reads 429 until the next day. A 429 is NOT unauthorized (do not expire the connection) and NOT a generic transient error (do not retry — retrying burns more quota).
fix: EnableBankingClient::transactions() returns 'rate_limited' on 429 (distinct from 'unauthorized'/null); request() skips HTTP retry on 401/403/429. ImportBankTransactions records a plain 'Limite giornaliero della banca raggiunto. Riprova domani.' and leaves the connection active; the daily schedule picks it up next run (idempotent, no data lost). Don't run manual imports/probes repeatedly against a low-quota bank.

title: Radix dialog slides in from top-left after the Tailwind v4 upgrade
symptoms: Modals open/close by sliding from the top-left corner to center instead of fading/zooming in place
Only centered dialogs are affected; tooltips/dropdowns animate fine
root_cause: tailwindcss-animate (the v3 plugin) is incompatible with Tailwind v4: its enter/exit keyframes set `transform` wholesale via translate3d/scale3d, which wipes DialogContent's `translate-x/y-[-50%]` centering while the animation runs. Radix content that centers itself with a translate loses that translate for the animation's duration and drifts from the corner.
fix: Replace tailwindcss-animate with its v4 successor tw-animate-css (@import 'tw-animate-css' in app.css), and remove the `slide-in-from-*`/`slide-out-to-*` classes from DialogContent so it animates with fade + zoom only (opacity/scale don't touch the centering transform). Leave tooltip/select slide classes as-is — they anchor to a trigger, not a centered transform.

title: Blank screen / 'Cannot read properties of null (reading component)' after the Inertia v3 upgrade
symptoms: White screen in the browser after upgrading to @inertiajs/react 3
Console: Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'component') at createInertiaApp
The server HTML clearly contains the page payload, yet the client sees initialPage as null
May be preceded by GET .../resources/js/app.tsx 404 if another Vite project holds port 5173
root_cause: Inertia v3 changed how the initial page payload is delivered: it now reads it from a `<script data-page="app" type="application/json">` tag (getInitialPageFromDOM), NOT from `<div id="app" data-page="...">` as in v2. The @inertia Blade directive in inertia-laravel v3 emits the new script form, but Laravel's compiled view cache still held the v2 directive output (the div-with-data-page), so getInitialPageFromDOM found no script tag and initialPage was null. A second, independent confounder: if another local Vite project already owns port 5173, the browser loads the wrong app.tsx/@inertiajs bundle entirely.
fix:
Clear Laravel's compiled views so the v3 @inertia directive regenerates: `php artisan view:clear` (also config:clear/cache:clear for good measure). Verify the served HTML now has `
` (empty div). Separately, ensure no other Vite dev server is holding port 5173 (stop it, clear node_modules/.vite, recreate the container). Consider pinning a non-default Vite port for this project to avoid the clash.

title: 404 on http://localhost:5173/resources/js/app.tsx — another project's Vite squats the port on IPv6 localhost
symptoms: Browser console: GET http://localhost:5173/resources/js/app.tsx net::ERR_ABORTED 404 (Not Found)
curl from the host returns 200 but with Content-Type: text/html (Vite's SPA index fallback) instead of text/javascript
Even a non-existent path like /resources/js/app.jsx returns 200 text/html — proof the responder has a different root
The same request from INSIDE the container returns 200 text/javascript
Clearing node_modules/.vite and restarting does not help
root_cause: A Vite dev server from an unrelated project (dice-engine) was listening on [::1]:5173 (IPv6 localhost) while Docker published only *:5173. Browsers and host curl resolve 'localhost' to ::1 first, so requests hit the foreign Vite, which has no resources/js/app.tsx and answers with its own SPA index.html. Worse, that server ran with strictPort:false, so it hopped onto the next free port (5174) as soon as this project claimed it — chasing the remapped port.
fix: Publish Vite on a host port far from the 5173-5174 range: docker-compose maps ${DEV_VITE_PORT:-5273}:5173 (container port stays 5173). Because the host port then differs from the container port, vite.config.ts must advertise the host port to the browser via server.origin and server.hmr.clientPort, both driven by VITE_DEV_CLIENT_PORT passed in from compose — otherwise Laravel emits working URLs but HMR connects to the wrong port. Diagnose with: lsof -nP -iTCP:5173 -sTCP:LISTEN (look for a node PID on [::1]) and compare curl localhost:PORT vs curl 127.0.0.1:PORT — differing content-types prove a port collision, not a Vite/Laravel bug.

title: Reading assets.value directly reports 0 for a quantity-held asset (ticker + quantity)
symptoms: a ticker asset shows a month-over-month change equal to its whole value (e.g. +10.546,45 on a 10.546,45 position) every single month
the same asset renders the correct figure elsewhere in the UI
SELECT value FROM assets returns 0.00 for the row while the app displays thousands
root_cause: For an asset held in units (ticker + quantity both set) the `value` COLUMN is left at 0 and the figure is derived at read time by Asset::currentValue($price) as quantity × current price. Any code that reads $asset->value instead of calling currentValue() therefore sees 0. FetchInputData::previousValues did exactly that, so every quantity-held asset compared a priced current value against a stored zero.
fix: Call currentValue($prices->get($a->ticker ?? '')?->price) instead of reading ->value; pass the AssetPrice collection the action already loads. Note the inherent limit: no historical prices are stored, so BOTH sides are priced at today's price and the month-over-month delta of a quantity-held asset reflects a change in QUANTITY (a contribution), never a price move. Regression-guarded by FetchInputDataTest::test_previous_value_of_a_quantity_held_asset_is_priced_not_read_from_the_column.

title: Vitest: userEvent.click hangs for 5s and times out under vi.useFakeTimers()
symptoms: A component test that pairs vi.useFakeTimers() with userEvent.setup() fails with 'Test timed out in 5000ms'
The test body never reaches its assertions; duration reads ~5015ms
The same click works fine in a sibling test that does not install fake timers
root_cause: userEvent's async API awaits internal delays on the real timer queue. Once vi.useFakeTimers() replaces the queue, nothing advances those delays and the click promise never settles. Passing userEvent.setup({ advanceTimers: vi.advanceTimersByTime }) does NOT reliably fix it in this repo's happy-dom setup.
fix: In tests that need fake timers, drive the interaction with fireEvent.click from @testing-library/react instead of userEvent — fireEvent is synchronous and timer-independent. Keep userEvent for the tests that assert interaction without stepping timers; both can coexist in one file. Step the component with act(() => vi.advanceTimersByTime(ms)) and restore with vi.useRealTimers() in afterEach.

title: A full-height page inside <main>'s scroll container loses its bottom padding
symptoms: A page laid out to fill the viewport (h-full p-4) has its last card run flush to the window bottom edge, with no gap, while the side/top gaps look correct
A short sibling column on the same page appears to have the gap, which misleads you into thinking the padding works and only one column is broken
Setting min-h-0 or switching h-full to an h-[calc(100%-2rem)] + my-4 does NOT fix it
root_cause: AppLayout's <main> is the scroll container (overflow-y-auto). A block child sized h-full becomes exactly as tall as that container, and a scroll container drops a filling child's bottom padding at the scroll end, so the padding renders outside the visible box. The short column only looked correct because its content ran out early, not because its padding was honoured.
fix: Make <main> a flex column (flex flex-col min-h-0), then have full-height pages use flex-1 min-h-0 instead of h-full: as a flex item the page is bounded by the real available height and its own padding stays inside. Pages that are meant to scroll must then be marked shrink-0, otherwise being a flex item compresses their long content instead of scrolling it.

title: min-h-[200px] on a flex child makes cards overflow onto their neighbours
symptoms: Chart cards in a grid row visibly paint over the cards in the row below
The page still scrolls even though every row was given a share of the leftover height
Cards refuse to get smaller no matter how the parent flex chain is sized
root_cause: min-height on a flex item overrides min-h-0 and blocks shrinking entirely: the item cannot go below its floor, so it overruns its grid row instead. Recharts' ResponsiveContainer minHeight={n} adds the same floor a second time.
fix: Use min-h-0 on the flexing CardContent and drop ResponsiveContainer's minHeight so the chart follows its box. Add overflow-hidden to each card as a clip guard. Where content genuinely cannot shrink (a fixed-size donut plus a legend that grows with the data), let that one card scroll internally instead.

title: is_manual cannot double as a "reviewed" flag: agreeing with the classifier never reaches the server
symptoms: A review queue built on is_manual never empties: rows the user looked at and agreed with keep coming back as new
Only the rows whose flow_type or excluded was actually changed ever get flagged
root_cause: Two independent reasons. (1) stage() in Cashflow.tsx deletes an edit when the value returns to the row's saved state and saveAll() posts only the edits Map, so 'the classifier said expense, that's right' produces zero changes and zero UPDATEs — and since the classifier is usually right, that is the majority of rows. (2) is_manual means 'the user overrode the machine, never reclassify' — ClassifyBankTransactions skips those rows forever — so reusing it as 'seen' would freeze the whole backlog against future classifier rules.
fix: A separate reviewed_at timestamp column. The client posts the month rather than a list of ids and the server marks every still-pending row of that month in one UPDATE, so rows hidden behind an active filter aren't left behind. Keep is_manual's narrow override meaning.

title: Filtering rows out of the Cashflow Inertia payload silently breaks the month's totals
symptoms: The month's net drops after adding a server-side row filter, and no longer matches the last point of the monthly flow chart
root_cause: The month totals are computed client-side in Cashflow.tsx's `summary` useMemo by iterating the `transactions` prop — it has to be client-side so the figures reflect staged unsaved edits. Any row the server withholds is therefore missing from the sum, not merely hidden.
fix: Send every row of the month with its state as a field (e.g. `reviewed`) and filter in the consuming component only. When changing this area, verify the month's net still equals the chart's last point before and after.

title: DialogHeader spills outside the panel when DialogContent uses p-0
symptoms: The dialog title is clipped on the left, reading as cut off mid-word
The close (X) button is covered or invisible
The header appears shifted up and out of the rounded panel
root_cause: This project's DialogHeader is customised beyond stock shadcn: it carries `sticky -top-6 -mx-6 -mt-6 px-6 pt-6` so it can sit flush against DialogContent's default p-6 padding. A dialog that overrides the content to p-0 (needed when the body must scroll edge to edge) leaves those -24px negatives pulling the header outside the panel. Adding padding to the header does not help — the negative margins have to be cancelled.
fix: On such a dialog pass `static mx-0 mt-0` to DialogHeader alongside its own padding, plus `pr-12` so the title clears the absolutely-positioned close button. Also re-assert `text-left`: the base is `text-center sm:text-left`.

title: VACUUM in a test fails, and the naive workaround wipes the whole suite
symptoms: 'cannot VACUUM from within a transaction' when a test exercises code calling VACUUM / VACUUM INTO
After switching the test to DatabaseMigrations: unrelated failure in a migration's down() ('error in index ... after drop column')
After overriding refreshTestDatabase(): 300+ unrelated tests fail with 'no such table: categories'
root_cause: RefreshDatabase wraps every test in a transaction (refreshTestDatabase() always calls beginDatabaseTransaction(); there is no opt-out flag), and SQLite refuses to VACUUM inside one. The two obvious escapes are both worse: DatabaseMigrations also runs the rollback, tripping a pre-existing down() that SQLite cannot execute; and overriding refreshTestDatabase() skips setting RefreshDatabaseState::$migrated, so every later test in the run shares an unmigrated in-memory database.
fix: Keep RefreshDatabase untouched and commit its transaction in the test's own setUp(): `while (DB::transactionLevel() > 0) { DB::commit(); }`. Migrations still run, the shared migrated-state bookkeeping stays intact, and isolation holds because the in-memory database is rebuilt per test. Scope this to the one test class that needs it.

title: Restoring a SQLite backup by copying only the .sqlite corrupts it via the stale WAL
symptoms: A page dies with 'SQLSTATE[HY000]: General error: 11 database disk image is malformed' after a restore, while other pages work fine
PRAGMA integrity_check reports 'Tree N page M cell K: invalid page number <huge>' on a couple of trees
SELECT COUNT(*) and full table scans succeed on the same tables that integrity_check flags, so the data looks intact
The failing query uses WHERE col IN (...) — an index lookup — while sequential reads over the same table pass
root_cause: The database runs in WAL mode (set in config/database.php), so database.sqlite-wal holds committed pages not yet checkpointed into the main file. Copying only the .sqlite over the live file leaves the previous database's -wal and -shm in place; on the next open SQLite replays that WAL over the restored file, splicing two unrelated database states together. Row data stays readable because the leaf pages are fine — only interior B-tree pointers go wrong, so the corruption hides until a query descends an index.
fix: Repair with dump-and-reload, which loses nothing when the rows are still readable: stop the container, copy the corrupt .sqlite AND its -wal/-shm aside, then in a keinos/sqlite3 container run `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`, `.dump` to SQL, and load into a fresh file; verify integrity_check plus per-table row counts against the corrupt file before promoting it. Expect the `cache` table to shrink (expired entries) — that is not data loss. To PREVENT it: always `rm -f database.sqlite-wal database.sqlite-shm` before copying a restored file into place, with the container stopped. backup:restore now prints this as a numbered procedure.

title: A fresh install lands on /login instead of /setup: middleware order, not middleware logic
symptoms: With zero users in the database, visiting any page redirects to /login rather than the first-run /setup page
The login page renders but cannot be got past — no account exists to log into, so the app is bricked on first run
The setup middleware itself is correct in isolation and its unit-level behaviour looks right
root_cause: Middleware appended to the web group with $middleware->web(append: [...]) does not thereby run before route middleware. Laravel sorts by its own priority list, in which Authenticate sits high, so `auth` rejected the guest and redirected to /login before RequireSetup ever ran and could divert to /setup.
fix: Declare the ordering explicitly with $middleware->priority([...]) in bootstrap/app.php, listing RequireSetup ahead of Illuminate\Auth\Middleware\Authenticate (the list must be complete — it replaces the framework default, so copy Laravel's and insert). Covered by tests/Feature/Auth/SetupTest::test_a_fresh_install_is_sent_to_setup, which is what caught it; the failure is invisible in local dev once an account exists, and would only reappear on a fresh deploy.

title: Password change appears to work but leaves other devices signed in
symptoms: Changing the password succeeds, yet a session on another device keeps working
Auth::logoutOtherDevices() runs without error and has no effect
remember_token still holds its old value after an update() that included it, so the long-lived 'remember me' cookie stays valid
root_cause: Two independent silent no-ops. (1) Auth::logoutOtherDevices() only invalidates other sessions when the AuthenticateSession middleware is active on the route; this app does not run it, so the call does nothing and reports nothing. (2) remember_token is not in User::$fillable, so passing it to update() is dropped by mass-assignment guarding without an error.
fix: Delete the other sessions directly — DB::table('sessions')->where('user_id', $id)->where('id', '!=', session()->getId())->delete() — which needs no extra middleware and is directly assertable in a test. Write remember_token with forceFill()->save() rather than update(); the 'hashed' cast still applies to password, which a test should pin since forceFill bypasses guarding. Verify with two real sessions: log in from two cookie jars, change the password from one, and assert the other is bounced to /login.

title: App reachable on the host but times out over Tailscale
symptoms: curl to localhost:8080 returns 200 on the server, but the same app times out from a phone on the same tailnet
The Tailscale MagicDNS name resolves and `tailscale status` shows the device online
No error in the container logs — the connection never arrives
root_cause: The compose port was published to 127.0.0.1 only. Traffic arriving over Tailscale lands on the tailnet interface (100.x.y.z), not on loopback, so Docker's localhost-only binding refuses it before the app sees anything.
fix: Publish the port on the tailnet address instead: docker-compose.prod.yml uses "${BIND_ADDRESS:-127.0.0.1}:8080:8000", so setting BIND_ADDRESS to the output of `tailscale ip -4` in .env fixes it. Recreate with --force-recreate (a restart does not re-read .env). Verify on the host with `curl http://$(tailscale ip -4):8080/up` before testing from the phone. Do NOT use 0.0.0.0 — that publishes to the whole LAN and defeats the point of a private network. The 127.0.0.1 default stays correct for a VPS, where a reverse proxy on the host forwards to loopback.

title: 419 Page Expired on every login when serving over plain HTTP
symptoms: Login POST returns 419 Page Expired; the page loads fine and the form renders
Happens over http:// on a private network (Tailscale, LAN) with APP_ENV=production
The error names CSRF, which sends you looking at tokens and middleware rather than cookies
root_cause: With APP_ENV=production and SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE unset, Laravel marks the session cookie `secure`, so the browser only sends it back over HTTPS. Over http:// the cookie never returns, the session is empty on the POST, and CSRF verification fails — reported as 419.
fix: Set SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE=false in .env when serving over plain HTTP, and recreate the container (`--force-recreate`; the prod entrypoint runs config:cache at startup, so a restart keeps the old values). Confirm with a runtime dump of config('session.secure') rather than reading .env. Behind Tailscale this is not a downgrade — WireGuard encrypts the transport — but set it back to true behind real HTTPS. Retry in a private window: a stale cookie from the broken origin reproduces the error against a fixed server. Related symptom on the same setup: APP_URL not matching the address actually opened.

title: sc login dies with a DBus error inside the container
symptoms: `sc login` fails immediately with 'Platform secure storage failure: DBus error: Using X11 for dbus-daemon autolaunch was disabled at compile time'
Happens in the prod container while the dev container logs in fine
The error mentions X11 and DBus, pointing at desktop plumbing rather than at configuration
root_cause: The Scalable CLI defaults to OS keyring storage, which talks to D-Bus — absent in a container. The dev compose command writes ~/.config/scalable-cli/config.toml selecting file-backed session and signing-key storage; docker/prod-entrypoint.sh was written without that step, so the prod image inherited the keyring default.
fix: The prod entrypoint now writes the same config.toml before anything can invoke the CLI (session_backend and signing_key_backend = "file"), creating it only when absent so an existing one in the scalable-cli volume is preserved. Verify by running `sc login` and checking it reaches the device-code prompt; the 'session secrets are stored in local files' warning is expected and is the intended mode. Note the config lives in the scalable-cli named volume, so it survives container recreation along with the login session itself.

title: A second Http::fake() in one test does not replace the first
symptoms: A test that fakes one response, acts, then fakes a different response and acts again sees the FIRST response both times
The assertion failure looks like a bug in the code under test — a state transition that never happens (e.g. a notification that is never cleared)
Running the same sequence by hand in tinker behaves correctly, which is the clue that the test harness is at fault
root_cause: Http::fake() registers stubs additively. Calling it again with the same URL pattern appends a second stub, and the first one keeps answering, so the intended second response is never returned.
fix: Model successive differing responses with Http::sequence(): build it with ->push() per call and register once via Http::fake(['host/*' => $sequence]). See fakeCompareSequence() in tests/Feature/Console/CheckForUpdatesTest.php. General lesson: when a test claims a state transition never happens, reproduce the transition outside the test (tinker, a real call) before changing the production code — here the code was correct from the start and two commits' worth of 'fixes' were nearly made to working logic.

title: Chart card is empty on a phone while an empty chart renders fine
symptoms: On a narrow viewport the dashboard shows chart card headers with nothing under them
A chart with NO data renders its empty state correctly, while the same chart WITH data shows nothing — the inverse of what a data bug looks like
Nothing is logged and the DOM contains the ResponsiveContainer, so it reads as a Recharts problem rather than a layout one
Desktop is perfect, which hides the bug from anyone not opening devtools at 375px
root_cause: Recharts' <ResponsiveContainer height="100%"> resolves against its parent, and the parent chain only supplied a height at lg: Pages/Dashboard.tsx wrapped the page in `lg:flex-1 lg:min-h-0` and each chart grid row in `lg:flex-1 lg:min-h-0`. Below lg those classes drop off, the row has auto height, the Card's `h-full` resolves to auto, CardContent's `flex-1 min-h-0` collapses, and 100% of 0 is 0. ChartEmptyState carried its own `height: 200` inline, which is why the empty branch was the only visible one.
fix: Give the chart Card an intrinsic mobile height and keep the desktop chain: `h-64 lg:h-full` on the <Card> in each of Components/Charts/*.tsx (AllocationDonutChart is excluded — it has no ResponsiveContainer and sizes to content). Fix it in the component, not at the call site, so a second consumer cannot inherit the bug. Corollary footgun found the same way: a wrapper with a fixed height must contain ONLY the chart — Advisor/Widgets/NetWorthLine.tsx wrapped chart + caption in one h-[240px] div, pushing the caption outside its own box. General rule: any `height="100%"` needs a bounded ancestor at EVERY breakpoint, so grep for `lg:`-only flex chains above one.

title: A p-0 dialog regains padding at sm: after DialogContent became responsive
symptoms: A dialog that deliberately scrolls edge to edge shows padding again above 640px, while looking correct on a phone
The sticky DialogHeader is flush on mobile and hangs outside the panel on desktop, or the reverse
Only dialogs that override padding are affected; every other dialog looks fine, so it reads as a one-off
root_cause: DialogContent's padding is now responsive — `p-4 sm:p-6` — and DialogHeader's cancelling negatives mirror it per breakpoint (`-top-4 -mx-4 -mt-4 px-4 pt-4` plus `sm:` variants). A dialog that passes a single unprefixed `p-0` only wins at the base breakpoint: `sm:p-6` from the primitive has the same specificity and comes later, so the padding returns at >=640px. Supersedes pb_20260804_183900_8c55, which described the older single `p-6`.
fix: Override BOTH breakpoints on any dialog that changes padding: `p-0 sm:p-0` on DialogContent, and on DialogHeader `static mx-0 mt-0 px-4 pt-4` plus `sm:mx-0 sm:mt-0 sm:px-4 sm:pt-4` (see Cashflow/TransactionsReviewDialog.tsx). Keep `pr-12` for the close button and re-assert `text-left`. The rule: DialogHeader's offsets exist only to cancel DialogContent's padding, so the two must be changed together at every breakpoint.

title: "Enable Banking non configurato" after moving to a new host: the .pem is a file, and it lives in the data directory
symptoms: Settings shows 'Enable Banking non configurato (chiave/credenziali mancanti)' although ENABLE_BANKING_APPLICATION_ID and the paths are set in .env
every bank account shows 'Ultimo sync fallito' / 'Saldo non disponibile'
storage/logs/laravel.log repeats 'Enable Banking private key file not accessible' followed by 'aspsps fetch failed {"status":null}'
the warning persists for up to 24h after the key is put in place
root_cause: ENABLE_BANKING_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH points at /app/storage/app/enable-banking.pem, i.e. inside the mounted data directory, so the key is host state like the database — not something .env carries. A host migration that copies .env and database.sqlite leaves the key behind, every JWT signing returns null, and aspsps() comes back empty. The UI derives 'non configurato' from an empty bank list (banks.length === 0 in BankConnectionsCard), so a network/auth failure is reported as missing credentials, pointing at the one thing that is correct. The empty list is then cached under enable_banking.aspsps.IT for a day, so the warning outlives the fix.
fix: Copy the .pem into the host data directory (chmod 600), confirm the container sees it, then forget the cached bank list: Cache::forget('enable_banking.aspsps.IT'). Verify with a live aspsps('IT') call returning a non-empty list rather than trusting the UI.
